Sam's beginner recipe — your very first loaf

Never baked sourdough before? This is the one Sam gives everyone first. Forgiving dough, no kneading, and a lovely crackly crust — you just need an active starter, a heavy pot with a lid, and a bit of patience.

Makes 1 loafAbout 24 hours, mostly waitingHands-on: ~30 minutesDifficulty: beginner

You'll need

  • 500g strong bread flour
  • 375g lukewarm water (75%)
  • 100g active sourdough starter — fed 4–8 hours ago, doubled and bubbly
  • 10g fine sea salt
  • A Dutch oven or heavy lidded pot

Before you start

No starter yet? Ask Sam “How do I make a starter?” in the chat above — he'll walk you through the week it takes, naming it included. If your starter hasn't doubled since its last feed, wait — a sleepy starter makes a flat loaf.

  1. Mix (morning). Stir the flour and water together until no dry flour remains. Cover and rest for 1 hour — that's the autolyse, and it does half the work for you.
  2. Add starter and salt. Mix them in with wet hands, squeezing and folding until it all comes together into a shaggy ball. Rest 30 minutes.
  3. Bulk ferment (3–4 hours). Leave the bowl somewhere warm. Four times during the first two hours, with wet hands, gently stretch one side of the dough up and fold it over — turn the bowl and repeat on all four sides. The dough should end up puffy, smooth and a bit wobbly.
  4. Shape. Tip the dough onto a lightly floured surface, fold the edges into the middle, flip it over and gently pull it towards you to tighten it into a round. Place it seam-side up in a well-floured bowl or basket.
  5. Cold proof (overnight). Cover and put it in the fridge for 12–16 hours. This is where the flavour — and that gentle tang — develops.
  6. Bake (next morning). Heat the oven and the pot at 230°C for 45 minutes. Turn the loaf out onto baking paper, score one confident slash across the top, and lower it into the hot pot. Bake 20 minutes with the lid on, then 20–25 minutes with the lid off, until deep golden.
  7. Wait (the hardest step). Cool on a rack for at least 1 hour before slicing — the inside is still finishing. Then tear in, butter generously, and be very proud of yourself.

sam's first-loaf promise — If it comes out a bit flat, it will still taste wonderful toasted. Tell Sam what happened in the chat and he'll help you fix it next time. Nobody's first loaf is their best loaf — that's rather the point.
